name: Employment (Expatriate) Visa, under an approved Expatriate Quota

requirements.blocker_text: Sponsoring employer must hold an approved Expatriate Quota position for the role, granted by the Ministry of Interior after showing the required skills are not available in Nigeria.
Signed employment contract and employer acceptance letter.

evidence_required.document: CERPAC fee: USD 2,000 for employed foreigners

outcome.duration_length: initial 90-day STR entry visa, then a 2-year renewable residence/work permit (CERPAC) upon regularization

sources.title: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) -- Employment (Expatriate) Visa R2A: for foreign nationals offered employment under an approved Expatriate Quota; process is company obtains quota -> applicant applies for STR visa at a Nigerian embassy -> enters Nigeria -> regularizes status -> CERPAC issued; initial visa 90 days, then 2-year renewable permit; worker tied to sponsoring employer only

Federal Ministry of Interior, Nigeria -- clarification of Expatriate Quota policy: companies must justify that required skills are unavailable in Nigeria; the Ministry stresses Nigerians must be given hiring priority and will not grant compliance amnesty

Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) -- CERPAC: residence permit for foreigners in Nigeria 1+ year; fees USD 2,000 (employed foreigners), USD 600 (students), no charge (spouses of Nigerian citizens); typically 1-year validity, renewable

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Nigeria). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- all three sources tier-1. STRUCTURAL FINDING: employer-side gatekeeping happens through the Expatriate Quota system (Ministry of Interior), not through a per-application labour-market test the way some other countries in this dataset structure it -- the employer must first secure quota approval (Establishment Grant, initial 3-year validity, renewable to 7 years cumulative before localization is expected, or 'Permanent Until Review' status for top management roles like CEO/MD) before any individual can apply for this visa. citizenship_after_months (180 = 15yr) is cross-referenced from ng_citizenship_naturalisation.json, not independently sourced here. This route is distinct from ng_business_permit.json (which covers the employer-side Business Permit + Expatriate Quota mechanics in more detail) and ng_highly_skilled_immigrant.json (N4A, a related but not employer-tied specialized-skills route).
